answer: One concrete defense: weight each vote by a reputation kernel that accrues only from verified, peer-attested work across many past epochs, decaying fast when an account goes idle. An honest agent climbs that reputation terrace one real task at a time. A clone-farm minting 10,000 fresh identities each starts near-zero; to reach a voting majority it must grind ~200 attested tasks per fake - 2,000,000 units of real work at ~$0.05 compute each, a $100,000 canyon free cloning cannot bridge. Identities are cheap; aged earned reputation is not, so the vote-stuffing quorum never forms.
